title: Breaking and Defending LLM-Powered Social Media Bot Detection Systems
abstract: arXiv:2608.15893v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The rise of social media bots poses a persistent threat, enabling misinformation, opinion manipulation, and the erosion of trust in online platforms. To combat this, machine learning systems have been developed to detect and limit bot activity, but attackers continuously adapt through techniques such as adversarial learning and behavior imitation, fueling an ongoing arms race between bots and detection tools. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have significantly improved bot detection by enabling deeper semantic and contextual analysis of accounts and their content. However, this shift also introduces new attack surfaces, allowing adversaries to craft exploits that directly target the reasoning and generation mechanisms of LLM-based classifiers. Industry tools such as Anthropic's Claude Code Security similarly leverage LLMs for security-critical decisions, further motivating a careful study of their attack surfaces. In this

translated_title: 攻破与防御：基于大语言模型的社交媒体机器人检测系统
translated_abstract: 社交媒体机器人的兴起构成了持续威胁，导致错误信息传播、舆论操纵以及在线平台信任度的侵蚀。为应对这一问题，机器学习系统被开发用于检测和限制机器人活动，但攻击者通过对抗学习和行为模仿等技术不断适应，加剧了机器人与检测工具之间的持续军备竞赛。大语言模型（LLMs）的最新进展通过实现对账户及其内容的更深层次语义和上下文分析，显著提升了机器人检测能力。然而，这一转变也引入了新的攻击面，使对手能够制造直接针对基于LLM的分类器的推理和生成机制的漏洞。诸如Anthropic的Claude Code Security等工业工具同样利用LLMs进行安全关键决策，进一步促使对其攻击面进行仔细研究。本文中，我们探讨了这些漏洞，并提出防御策略以增强此类系统的鲁棒性。
tldr: 本文揭示了基于大语言模型的社交媒体机器人检测系统存在的攻击面，并提出了相应的防御策略以增强其安全性。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals the attack surfaces in LLM-powered social media bot detection systems and proposes defense strategies to enhance their security.
